name: tiny-tls (demo)
story: Heartbleed (2014): a buffer over-read in OpenSSL exposed the memory of two thirds of the web to anyone who asked. OpenSSL was maintained by a handful of volunteers on roughly $2,000 a year in donations, with one full-time developer.

name: stream-utils (demo)
story: event-stream (2018): the burnt-out maintainer handed the package to a stranger who offered to help. The new owner shipped a payload that stole Bitcoin wallets. The package had ~2 million weekly downloads and zero funding.

name: log-helper (demo)
story: Log4Shell (2021): one line in Log4j gave remote code execution across millions of Java servers. Three unpaid volunteers spent their holidays patching it while the world waited.

name: color-text (demo)
story: colors.js / faker.js (2022): the author, tired of large companies profiting from his unpaid work, pushed an infinite loop on purpose. Thousands of builds broke overnight — including Amazon's and Facebook's.

name: compress-lite (demo)
story: xz backdoor (2024): an attacker spent two years building trust as a helpful contributor, took co-maintainership of a compression library from an overwhelmed solo maintainer, and planted an SSH backdoor that nearly reached every Linux distribution.
